keywords_en: criminal; crime of theft; second instance; High People's Court; Henan Province; natural person; criminal law; whether the sentence is too severe; whether constitutes recidivism; whether constitutes especially serious circumstances; affirm the original judgment; theft of cultural relics; recidivism; death penalty sentence; theft
full_text_en:
Chen Heyi Theft Case

Defendant: Chen Heyi, male, 38 years old, farmer of Chenzhuang Village, Chengguan Town, Shangshui County, Henan Province. In 1973, Chen Heyi was sentenced to five years' imprisonment for theft; in 1982, he was again sentenced to one year's imprisonment for theft, suspended for one year; in 1984, he was again sentenced to one year's imprisonment for theft; after his sentence was completed and he was released, on November 23, 1985, he was arrested again for theft.

The defendant Chen Heyi was indicted for theft by the Zhoukou Branch of the Henan Provincial People's Procuratorate before the Zhoukou Intermediate People's Court. After accepting the case, the Zhoukou Intermediate People's Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, and after a public trial, found the following facts:

At approximately 11:00 p.m. on the night of November 5, 1985, the defendant Chen Heyi sneaked into the courtyard of the Shangshui County Cultural Center, pried off the door latch of the cultural relics storeroom with pliers, and entered the room to steal seven cultural relics, including two Grade 2 cultural relics: one Western Zhou bronze gui (food vessel) and one Song Dynasty porcelain recumbent-ox water dropper; three Grade 3 cultural relics: one Tang Dynasty tri-color glazed porcelain censer, one Song Dynasty double-persimmon-shaped water dropper, and one Song Dynasty black-flowered porcelain bowl; and two ordinary cultural relics: one Han Dynasty bronze belt hook and one Ming Dynasty imitation of a Han jade belt hook. He also stole one modern craft item, a Tang-style imitation porcelain horse. After the case was solved, all of the above stolen cultural relics were seized and recovered.

The above criminal facts were confirmed by the on-site investigation records, technical identifications, physical evidence, and witness testimony, and the defendant Chen Heyi also confessed to them.

The Zhoukou Intermediate People's Court, after trial, held that the defendant Chen Heyi had been sentenced to imprisonment for theft three times previously, and shortly after his release upon completion of the sentence, he again stole precious cultural relics of the state, and his conduct constituted the crime of theft as stipulated in Article 152 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. Chen Heyi, having been sentenced to one year's imprisonment for theft in 1984 and, within three years after his release upon completion of the sentence, having again committed a crime punishable by fixed-term imprisonment or more, was a recidivist according to the provisions of Article 61, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, and should be given a heavier punishment. Chen Heyi's theft of precious cultural relics of the state was of an especially vile nature and the circumstances were especially serious. In accordance with the provisions of Item (1) of Article 1 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress Regarding the Severe Punishment of Criminals Who Seriously Sabotage the Economy, he should be severely punished. Accordingly, on May 29, 1986, the court sentenced the defendant Chen Heyi to death for the crime of theft, and, in accordance with the provisions of Article 53, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, deprived him of political rights for life.

After the first-instance judgment, the defendant Chen Heyi appealed to the Henan High People's Court on the grounds that the sentence was too heavy.

The Henan High People's Court, after trial, held that the facts of the crime as found by the original trial regarding the appellant Chen Heyi were clear, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, the conviction was accurate, the sentence was appropriate, and the trial procedures were lawful. The grounds of appeal of the appellant Chen Heyi could not be established. On August 3, 1986, in accordance with the provisions of Item (1) of Article 136 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and after deliberation by the Adjudication Committee, it ruled to reject the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The Henan High People's Court, in accordance with the provisions of the Supreme People's Court authorizing high people's courts to approve the death penalty in certain cases, approved the judgment of the Zhoukou Intermediate People's Court sentencing Chen Heyi to death for the crime of theft and depriving him of political rights for life.
